$comment: CONFIGURE TIME ONLY — never read at run time, and not installed (cmake/DssInstall.cmake excludes this directory; the install smoke test proves the installed compiler compiles without it). `maxNesting` is the deepest a DSS config document may nest, its own top-level container counted as level 1: every reader takes it (`parseConfigDocument`, core/types/config_document_parse.hpp), so a deeper document is refused by name, at the pointer of its first container past the limit, before any loader walks it. It cannot live in a document the compiler reads at run time, because it governs the reading of every config document, that one's included: CMake reads it when the build is configured (cmake/DssConfigNestingLimit.cmake, refusing by name a missing document, one that is not a JSON object, or a `maxNesting` that is not a positive whole number) and compiles it in (src/core/CMakeLists.txt); the library refuses to build without that forward, so no default in code stands in for it. THE VALUE (cycle P69 L2, lane `lm`): 64 = four times the deepest shipped document (15 levels, sources/c.lang.json, MEASURED 2026-10-20 over every document of this tree), and within what the grammar loader's still-recursive walks take on a 1 MiB stack (INFERRED). The loader's nine recursive walks move onto work stacks in the lane's next item (L2b), whose test loads a document nested to this limit on a small stack; L2b revisits this value then, so that the bound reflects the work-stack design, not today's recursion.
